Statutory Biodiversity Duty Delivery Report (2012–2014)

This report details how East Dunbartonshire Council delivered biodiversity conservation across a range of functions between January 2012 and December 2014, fulfilling requirements under the Nature Conservation (Scotland) Act 2004 and the Wildlife and Natural Environment (Scotland) Act 2011.

  • Governance & Mainstreaming: Biodiversity conservation is embedded within Council functions, supported by the Single Outcome Agreement (SOA) and the Local Biodiversity Action Plan (LBAP 2010-2013).
  • Partnership Working: Collaborative projects include the East Dunbartonshire Green Gym, Glazert Water Pilot Project, and participation in the Kilpatricks and Campsie Green Network Steering Groups.
  • Communication & Education: Countryside rangers delivered 254 formal environmental education sessions and over 200 public events over the three-year period.
  • Community & Volunteer Engagement: Volunteers contributed over 1,000 work days annually, undertaking habitat management, pond creation, and invasive species removal alongside active 'Friends of' groups.
  • Directorate Actions: Specific initiatives span all Council directorates, ranging from wildflower planting for air quality improvement to eco-schools programs, local nature reserve proposals, peatland restoration, and sustainable procurement practices.

East Dunbartonshire Biodiversity Duty Delivery Report

This report from the Director of Development & Regeneration was presented to the Development & Regeneration Committee on 27 January 2015. It seeks approval for the first East Dunbartonshire Biodiversity Duty Delivery Report covering the period from January 2012 to December 2014, in compliance with the Nature Conservation (Scotland) Act 2004 and the Wildlife and Natural Environment (Scotland) Act 2011.

  • Statutory Duty: Public bodies must publish a report every three years detailing actions taken to further the conservation of biodiversity.
  • Key Initiatives (2012-2014):
    • Rehabilitation of degraded peat bog at six sites via the national Green Stimulus Peatland Restoration Project.
    • 92% of primary and secondary schools received an eco-schools award.
    • Mugdock Countryside Rangers led over 1,000 volunteer conservation work days annually.
    • Establishment of the East Dunbartonshire Green Gym in partnership with TCV Scotland.
    • Flood mitigation work at Colquhoun Park using environmental engineering techniques.
    • Over 250 environmental education sessions delivered to local school children.
  • Local Biodiversity Action Plan (LBAP): The 2010-2013 LBAP covers both East and West Dunbartonshire and is scheduled for an update in 2015.
  • Recommendations: The Committee was recommended to note the achievements, approve the 2012-2014 report for submission to the Scottish Government and publication on the Council website, and investigate the development of a framework to monitor biodiversity duties across all Council services.
